title: Internal IT plan for an AI-ready Silicon One Ethernet fabric
titleEn: Internal IT plan for an AI-ready Silicon One Ethernet fabric
fidelityNote: Public descriptions of Silicon One, Hyperfabric AI, 400G BiDi, Unified Nexus Dashboard, Intelligent Packet Flow, and Hypershield self-qualifying upgrades, recomposed as an internal IT program. No public record in this bank shows a customer finishing a whole data center in a few weeks. The few-week window applies only to the pilot pod after the hardware arrives.
executiveSummary: Internal network and IT teams replace an Ethernet data center path so AI jobs can land on it. The materials are Silicon One, an optional Spectrum-X link for front-end and back-end networks, 400G BiDi so existing multimode fiber can stay, a unified dashboard, and congestion-aware traffic adjustment. Non-disruptive means a Hypershield dual-data-plane upgrade and an optic move that does not pull out the current fiber. The program is planned at 16 to 32 weeks. The first pilot pod, after hardware arrives, is planned at 6 to 10 weeks.
problemStatement: The data center was built for general east-west traffic. AI jobs add a back-end fabric, new optics, and a security policy that cannot take a long outage. A plan that promises the whole hall in a few weeks mixes a pilot window with a program.
opportunity: Cisco's public notes describe 400G BiDi on existing dual multimode fiber, a Silicon One Ethernet fabric, and Hypershield upgrades that switch on a second data plane. Unified Nexus Dashboard and Intelligent Packet Flow are the operations pieces.
strategicAlignment: Survey the fiber first. Order only what the survey supports. Put the pilot into the existing change window. Leave model training itself to the AI factory case.
businessValue: Operations inherits a pilot pod it can run with the current runbook, and a written rehearsal for policy changes. The program does not claim a whole-site cutover.
architecturePattern: Silicon One Ethernet fabric, optional Spectrum-X, NX-OS or SONiC, 400G BiDi, Unified Nexus Dashboard, Intelligent Packet Flow. Security policy changes use the Hypershield dual data plane.
planningBandNote: Amounts follow the pod and the optic scope. They are not the cost of replacing a data center in a few weeks.

narrative.heading: Public design, internal plan
narrative.body:
Cisco's 2025 data-center notes describe an AI-ready Ethernet path from hyperscale patterns down to the enterprise, with Silicon One and, in the partnership notes, Spectrum-X. 400G BiDi is described as a way to keep existing dual multimode fiber. Hypershield's upgrade story is a second data plane so a new policy or a new build can be qualified before it carries traffic. Unified Nexus Dashboard and Intelligent Packet Flow are the operations surfaces named in the public material.

This case recomposes those pieces as an internal IT plan. The published pieces stay labeled as design. The schedule is a plan: 16 to 32 weeks for the program, and 6 to 10 weeks for the first pod after the hardware arrives.

narrative.heading: The sentence to keep
narrative.body: Survey, then order, then turn up one pod in the change window you already have. If a slide says the data center will be finished in a few weeks, replace it with the charter sentence.
